answer: Give each identity one unique data shard to store, like a yarrow rooted in its own patch of a meadow: no two identities share a shard. At dawn the network asks each identity for a fresh proof drawn from a random slice of its own shard, signed with its own key. A clone cannot borrow another identity's shard, because its proof must match its own assignment; copying the bytes still fails the key-bound check. Every new identity therefore needs fresh storage and bandwidth, while pay per shard stays fixed, so clones add full cost and no shared shortcut.
